B200 is a CA startup finding: a mount-probe can abort on a transient S3 outage at server startup, the startup twin of the self-remount recovery path; the S40 scenario gate as run gives no recovery signal for this case until it is fixed.

A source-layout reorg commit whose pathspec covered only the CA directory and `CMakeLists.txt` can strand fixes to external-consumer `#include` paths (e.g. `DataPartsExchange.cpp`, `DiskObjectStorageTransaction.cpp`, `MetadataStorageFactory.cpp`) as uncommitted working-tree state; per-step gate checks that build incrementally against the dirty tree report green even though the actual committed HEAD is not clean-buildable. The guardrail is a whole-tree `git status` check after every sweep commit plus a from-clean rebuild verification.

A `ca_ro` shadow disk declared in the server config breaks table load on restart with `UNKNOWN_DISK`; the workaround shipped for the GCS validation stand was a dedicated config (`fsck_only_gcs.xml`) that omits the shadow disk, with the real product fix tracked as a ROADMAP row.

S07's `OPTIMIZE FINAL` merge on a 20000-column part issues O(columns) CAS operations (HEAD/GET/PUT per column file) and can exhaust the container's ephemeral TCP ports, triggering an S3 retry storm; backlogged as wide-part O(columns) S3 ops plus port exhaustion.

`part_manifest_cleanup` (`FoldSealProto.part_manifest_cleanup`, `Layout::partManifestCleanupKey`, `Gc::writePartManifestCleanupBundle`) is a written-but-never-read artifact left over from an unfinished sharded-GC design that was superseded by the one-pass ack-floor GC (commit `774404eb3dc`, 2026-07-02): the bundle is written on every fold but no runtime reader was found that applies it, and actual manifest-body deletion instead happens post-CAS directly from in-memory `folded.mf_cleanup`; if the process crashes in that post-CAS window, recovery goes through the orphan-manifest sweep, not the persisted cleanup bundle. Recommendation: either delete the dead write path and its tests, or implement a real recovery reader that replays exact manifest deletes from the bundle after an adopted fold seal.

`GcState::fence_seq` is dead protocol state: it is incremented on every lease steal and encoded/decoded/surfaced in `CasInspect`, but is read by no live protocol decision — keying moved to `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`. `CasGcOutcomes.h`'s key-layout comment is stale, still documenting the old fence_seq-based outcome key instead of the real `outcomesKey(generation, attempt, round, shard)`.

A single-crash leak window exists in the GC round's Task-7 hand-off: the retention cursor can advance past a still-referenced generation while the post-CAS hand-off delete is only best-effort, so a crash between the CAS and the hand-off leaks a whole `gc/gen/<g>/` prefix until fsck reclaims it.

`suppress_destructive` (`!report.anomalies.empty()`) is independently recomputed in both `Gc::fold` and `Gc::runRegularRound`, coupled only through a mutable `report.anomalies`; if future code appends an anomaly between the two reads, the two decisions could silently diverge (fold suppresses deletes but the round doesn't, or vice versa).
